name: Multicam Cut in One Node
description: Edit a podcast filmed on several cameras with a single node: Tighten Episode lines the recordings up, transcribes the master audio, works out which camera each speaker is on, tightens the episode and cuts to whoever is talking, rendering a 720p Preview first. The sound stays on the master track throughout. Review it, then Render final renders the episode at full quality.

data.text:
Multicam Cut in one node

Drop a file on each recording node, then Run Tighten Episode. It lines the recordings up, transcribes the master audio, works out which camera each speaker is on, plans the trims and cuts each stretch to whoever is talking, rendered as a 720p Preview. The sound always comes from the master; only the picture switches. Review it (you can edit the cut), then choose Render final on Tighten Episode: it puts the cameras on your edited cut again and renders the full-quality episode.

To skip the review, turn off Tighten Episode's Review before render.

Captions are off; turn them on in its settings to add word-highlight captions at Render final.

Want to adjust each step yourself? The Multicam Cut template builds the same chain node by node.
data.label: Sticky Note

data.text:
The recordings

Recordings: Camera 1, Camera 2 and Wide Camera are wired into Tighten Episode's Recordings, in that order (drag them in its Recordings list to reorder). More cameras (up to 6 recordings in all, Master audio included): add an Upload Video node and wire it into Recordings. Every recording node needs a file before you run.

Master audio: the mixer or recorder track, wired into Master audio. It is the episode's sound and the clock the cameras are lined up to.

Wide camera: the camera that shows everyone (here the third recording). A speaker with no camera of their own is shown on it.

Who is on which camera: Speaker Map decides it from the cameras' own microphones. Speaker 1 is the first voice heard, Speaker 2 the next. When a speaker had no clear camera, the node says so under its result and shows them on the wide camera; set them to a camera in its Cameras settings to override the automatic map.
